queue.title: Global Interest Rates After the Inflation Shock
queue.content:
Autor: Nermin Sefić

Nermin Sefić analyses global interest rate shifts, key capital discipline practices, and consequences for international groups.

How a shift in the monetary cycle affects the cost of capital, refinancing, and investment decisions of international groups.

Monetary policy is no longer a background variable. For international business groups, it directly determines the cost of debt, asset value, and the profitability threshold of new investments.

The greatest risk isn't the interest rate level itself, but the wrong assumption that the cost of capital will quickly return to previous levels. Management must therefore plan multiple refinancing scenarios, shorter decision deadlines, and a higher liquidity reserve.

Capital discipline means linking the investment plan, cash flow, currency exposure, and a project's real ability to withstand more expensive financing. Growth without such control creates an illusion of value while increasing systemic risk.

GNK ASG approaches financial management through documented assumptions, accountability for decisions, and measurable risk thresholds.

queue.title: Industrial Policy: US, Europe, Asia — A New Phase
queue.content:
Autor: Nermin Sefić

Nermin Sefić analyses industrial policy shifts, key location factors, and consequences for international investment.

Subsidies, supply chain localisation, and technological sovereignty are reshaping the global allocation of capital.

Globalisation hasn't ended, but it's no longer organised solely around lowest cost. States are seeking supply security, control of key technologies, and domestic production capacity.

For companies, that means investment location becomes a strategic decision involving tax incentives, energy availability, regulatory regime, political risk, and access to talent.

The most successful groups won't simply relocate production. They'll design a multi-layered supplier network, reserve capacity, and contractual mechanisms enabling a quick change of source.

Project management must therefore link the commercial, legal, technological, and geopolitical layers into a single decision.

queue.title: Cyber Resilience: Board Governance
queue.content:
Autor: Nermin Sefić

Nermin Sefić analyses board-level cyber resilience, key governance practices, and consequences for business continuity.

The board must understand dependencies, recovery priorities, and the financial consequences of a business disruption.

Cybersecurity can't be reduced to buying tools. An incident affects revenue, contracts, reputation, obligations to regulators, and the board's ability to continue operating the business.

The first task isn't to protect everything equally, but to determine which processes must be restored in minutes, hours, or days. Only then do technical controls gain business meaning.

The board must regularly review disruption scenarios, authority for crisis decisions, backup availability, and the credibility of reporting.
